Kwashiorkor - Starving to death

By: Tarryn Crossman | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Summary:
A nation that starves its children starves itself

It's a condition associated with children in OTHER poor African countries, not South Africa.
But Kwashiorkor or Severe acute malnutrition killed 15 000 South Africa children between 2022 and 2023.  
15 000 children under 5 died a horrible, painful death, they starved to death. Starved to death in a country where government officials are earning multimillion rand salaries, 1.5 trillion was stolen by corruption in 5 years, and where 10.5 million tons of edible food is just thrown away every year.
This isn't happening in some far away land, it's in your country. Our children are dying

We go to a clinic in Tholeni village, near Butterworth in the eastern cape where 7 children died of SAM over a three month period last year, to find 100 small children being treated for malnutrition. We speak to the head nurse and meet a mom fighting daily to get food for her children. - I will have more details on this after my visit on Monday

It's a multifaceted issue, which is going to require state and private intervention to solve, but the SAHRC says there is no more time for failing policies and empty promises. They are calling for a state of disaster in the eastern cape specifically, Eileen says the only way to get on top of this is to set up a war room and bring all the stake holders into one space for at least a year of immediate action. Our children have no more time for meetings that go nowhere.

South Africa's stunting rate is at 27% which means nearly 6 million children, the future of our nation, will not reach their full cognitive and physical potential. Perpetuating the cycle of poverty and preventing our country from growing economically.
This isn't about social development, it's about investing in the future of our country. Experts are saying - Solving malnutrition will help solve unemployment, because children will become adults able to learn and gain employment.

We go to tertiary hospital the Frere and spend time in the paediatric ward with HOD kim Harper, this is where children land up when SAM has all but destroyed their tiny bodies. This is the last frontier, Harper says they lose more children than he wants to admit because by the time they get to him they have been malnourished for a long time, and have a range of other communicable diseases that their tiny bodies just can't fight anymore.
"Even if we stabilise them, their bodies are so destroyed by malnutrition that the long term damage is severe." but saving their lives is just the first step, they then still have to be sent home to the situation that landed them in hospital in the first place.
"It's a social problem and if they get out of the hospital these children have a lot of hardship ahead of them"

So who do we hold accountable, throughout the piece experts in the field will lay out the problem across the board, but one thing everyone keeps saying is that there is simply not enough money.
The child grant has to be raised to the poverty line.
We confront DSD in the Eastern Cape on their underspending in the last financial year, which is insane if you look at the stats of hunger and unemployment. And on their failure to spend over 67 million in a covid relief grant

Nolwazi Mbambani is a single mom to three girls, they live out here in a village about 20km from Butterworth.
she is HIV positive, unemployed, and alone in her daily fight against the trauma of poverty.

they are starving because they have been abandoned by their father, now I am their mother and father, I am everything.

Nolwazi
how many days do you go without food?
Sometimes, it is a week,
do you do when you are hungry?
I drink water.

You drink water for five days?

Nolwazi and her children are being denied their constitutional right to food, by a provincial government that seems to have forgotten what its job is.

do you sometimes sacrifice your food for the kids when it is not enough)
Yes so that they can eat.

With a high viral load, Nolwazi was warned not to breastfeed her daughter as there is a risk of transmission. But after days with no food, all she had to ease her daughter's starvation was breastmilk. Nolwazi made the hardest decision any mother could make, she breastfed her daughter, risking infection, rather than watching her go hungry for another day


I was trying
I had no choice, I had no money to buy milk

Her and daughter inside


I feel like I killed my baby I am so sorry This is not your fault Nolwazi You had no choice
FADE TO BLACK




South Africa is facing a crisis, as unemployment and poverty continue to rise, so does hunger. Last year alone 15 000 children nationwide were hospitalized for severe acute malnutrition or SAM. With an unemployment rate of 60%, the Eastern Cape is one of the hardest-hit provinces. We travel to the OR Tambo district, where 22 children died in just a few months


Up until a few years ago, life was good for Siphokazi Ncaza, but after losing her job in Cape Town , she was forced to return home to her village in the former Transkei. Here unemployment is rife and every day is a battle to feed her 11 month old son

How many days do you and your children go without food?
We can go a week without any food.
A whole week.
Yes.
I don’t feel good at all
I sometimes think to myself that I wish I were not alive rather than living as poor as I am.

Corene Conradie
That's the reality we see in South Africa and the Eastern Cape, and it's growing. The number of children dying is increasing daily. The number of people who face food insecurity is growing daily.

Gift of the Givers is the largest disaster response NGO in Africa, and they are the ones on the ground trying to provide food to curb the malnutrition crises across South Africa
In the eastern cape they are feeding nearly 23,000 people per day in their soup kitchens. Corene conradie is the regional co-ordinator

Corene Conradie
I would describe malnutrition in the Eastern Cape as a disaster that needs or requires immediate intervention because when we talk about malnutrition, we talk about children slowly dying because of lack of food.
Corene Conradie
based on what you see in these villages, do you think the government is doing enough?
Definitly Not.

Siphokazi’s son has been diagnosed with moderate to severe malnutrition and has to be constantly monitored at the local clinic

Sipho - He lost weight as time passed because I sometimes had money to buy him food, and other days I didn’t.
He is being assessed here by the head Nurse Nhlanhla Radebe

Nhlanhla: The baby didn’t gain weight at all
Since the last time

Nhlanhls is clear that if the child didn’t gain weight before his next visit he would have to be hospitalized

NHLANHLA
Sometimes, I find it difficult to catch those who are malnourished. When I find them, some of them are close to severe.

When the children arrive at the clinic Nhlanhla says he often has nothing to treat the malnutrition, no nutrient-dense supplements, no formula and no food

I have nothing to give.
I couldn’t do anything, my hands were tied.
You send them away empty-handed with a hungry child?
Yup. It is just frustrating, and painful.

The clinic is just one of many with little to no resources to treat malnourished children, according to Corene.

Corene Conradie
The head of the clinic, together with his staff, is the one who has to look these people in the eye, not knowing.
if that patient can return next week because, like I said, malnutrition.
You do face death.

Nolwazi and her daughters rely solely on the child support grant to survive, which is 510 rand per child.

(Ithatha ixesha elingakanani igranti uphela?)
Hayi lusuku olunye.
(How long do you have grant money for?)
Just one day.
14:32-14:50

(xa ufumana imali ye granti uthenge ukutya kuhlala ixesha elingakanani?)
kuhlala iiveki ezimbini. Emveni koko kushiyeka mhlamb omilimili izishebo zingabikho zibe ziphelile ndizame kengok isishebo.
(how long does the food bought using grant money last you?)
just two weeks
14:52-15:41

13 million children rely on the child support grant to eat, and While a basket of groceries has increased by 8% this year, the grant has risen by less than 1%.
It remains substantially lower than the bread poverty line.


Eileen Carter
when we asked, " Do you think the child support grant should be increased, one of the representatives of the Department of Health said it's a no-brainer, and it means that we've had these recommendations for a while now. We know the child support grant has not kept up with food inflation, so it needs more.

During Covid The Eastern Cape Department of Social Development was given over 100 million rands for urgent food relief, in 2022 they returned 67 million because they were unable to spend it before the end of the financial year.

This together the death of 120 children in 11 months in the eastern cape, triggered A Human Rights Commission enquiry into the province's malnutrition crises, headed by DR Eileen carter

EC
we called stakeholders to the table: the Department of Education, Social Development, Treasury
We have found that the rights to dignity of children are being violated. We have found that the fundamental interests of the children are not being accounted. When we return money to the fiscus

Eileen Carter
children are dying from preventable causes.
There's no time for us to waste here.
That's why we're calling for a state of disaster.

According to the commission’s report many government departments are accountable for the dire state of these children, but the Eastern Cape Department of Social Development returning 67 million in 2022. Which was meant for food, is unfathomable.
we drove to East London to meet WITH the Head of the department Mzimkhulu Machemba

So why did you send the 67 million rands back
Mzimkhulu Machemba
During COVID, the government provided money for food parcels. And we went through a procurement process. but in the middle of delivery, we realised
Mzimkhulu Machemba
this service provider is not going to be able to deliver
Mzimkhulu Machemba
and we are not going to spend this money.
Govan
What about the people who are waiting for the food? What consideration was made for them?
Mzimkhulu Machemba
Unfortunately, the system of government works with compliance, and compliance works with compliance.
Govan
Do you believe that malnutrition is is that crisis levels in the Eastern Cape.
Mzimkhulu Machemba
I'll be very careful with responding with a yes or no to your answer because I don't know what's behind it.
Govan
What does that mean? I'm talking here about 120 children dying over a thousand. They're severely malnourished. It's not a game of chess. I'm talking about children dying. Do you believe that this is a crisis in the Eastern Cape?
Mzimkhulu Machemba
I believe that malnutrition is a very serious problem and government has put in place mechanisms to deal with malnutrition.

So far for this financial year just over 930 food parcels have been distributed in the eastern cape

Govan
How many food parcels the Department of Social Development in the Eastern Cape gives annually?
Govan
Can you estimate for you 2000?
Mzimkhulu Machemba
3000, you want to run away? We don't have.
Govan
That's a devastating figure
Mzimkhulu Machemba
We don't have money.
Mzimkhulu Machemba
There's no money. There must be more money.

It's hard to hear there is no money for starving children from a provincial government where only 3 of its 39 municipalities received clean audits in the last year financial year
The Human Rights Commission has given the Eastern Cape provincial government 3 months to respond to their most urgent recommendation.

SAHRC
Dr. Unni, or if the government does nothing, what if they know to report and shelve it?
That would be a very sad day for the children of this country. But the Human Rights Commission also has some muscle.

As part of their humanitarian aid Gift of the Giver distributes 1500 food packages a month in the Eastern Cape. Once they were alerted to the dire state of hunger in and around the ndabakazi clinic they immediately responded with 100 care packages

These food parcels are life-saving in South Africa, where 27% of children are stunted, meaning they will never reach their full potential, perpetuating the cycle of poverty.

But where is the state; why is this burden falling on private organizations like gift of the givers?

CORNENE
We contacted the Department of Social Development
They basically told us that they don't do the food parcels.
we can't waste time looking at what government does and what they don't do, because the reality is people are dying and we can't sit back while children on a daily basis are dying, not because of a severe illness, but just because of lack of food.

Corene - Siphakazi you have a parcel

Nolwazi and Siphokazi both received packages that will get them through december



Gift of the givers has pledged to supply Nolwazi with formula and bulk food until her and her daughter are strong again.

"Even if we stabilise them, their bodies are so destroyed by malnutrition that the long term damage is severe." but saving their lives is just the first step, they then still have to be sent home to the situation that landed them in hospital in the first place. "It's a social problem and if they get out of the hospital these children have a lot of hardship ahead of them" So who do we hold accountable, throughout the piece experts in the field will lay out the problem across the board, but one thing everyone keeps saying is that there is simply not enough money. The child grant has to be raised to the poverty line. We confront DSD in the Eastern Cape on their underspending in the last financial year, which is insane if you look at the stats of hunger and unemployment. And on their failure to spend over 67 million in a covid relief grant
